  ? Sigil: should marks use CriticMarkup, an existing plain-text review convention: {==marked       
    text==}{>>jhf: why this?<<} for a comment or question, with a request tagged {>>jhf request:    
    shorten<<}? Or do you want a hug-specific sigil?

  ? History file: one append-only history.md per task in its files (.hug/tasks/p/p87ngv/history.md),
    linked from the ticket, with each resolved mark as a dated entry quoting the original text, the 
    exchange and the change made. Is that the right name and shape?                                 
    └ question 5 · crab · 1 min ago · answer                                                        
                                                                                                    
DESCRIPTION                                                                                         
The ticket stays the crisp working document. A person or agent marks a piece of a task's text with  
a comment, question or request that sits inline in the text, visible as text, with a recognizable   
sigil. The agent picks marks up, acts or answers, and resolves each by rewriting the ticket text    
to the clarified result and removing the mark. The dialogue that led there (the mark, replies, who  
and when) is appended to a history file attached to the task, never kept in the ticket.             
                                                                                                    
PURPOSE

│ chat history. Otherwise, the ticket will become bloated. The ticket has to stay crisp and clear.  
│ So I think the questions and requests might need replacement, but they might appear in the text   
│ so you can actually see them, just like text. We have to choose the sigils or how to recognize    
│ them and act on them. And then, as they are resolved, the ticket is changed, and any history or   
│ chat history is put into another document outside of the ticket. If we try to scram everything    
│ into the ticket, I think it will be like if you make threads inside the ticket, it will become    
│ bloated. And especially when things are complex, you will have longer and more intense chats,     
│ which will bloat them even more. When what you need is clarity. And clarity is often to find the  
│ succinctness in things and boil it down to its essence, not adding more text. So the text is the  
│ tool to which we reach short clarity very often. That's why the messy part has to go out into a   
│ different file. But I think the working document is the ticket itself. That's where the replies   
│ come, it's picked up, and then the AI gets an instruction to lead with clarity in the ticket,     
│ answer requests, do them, post any questions, and then put all of the prehistory provenance into  
│ a suitably named asset that can grow with a penned
